PT-00114 (TCAP-1): The Stress-Pathway Peptide That Targets Cortisol at Its Source — Research Dossier

Research compounds discussed for educational purposes. Not FDA-approved for human use where applicable. Consult a healthcare provider before use.

What Is PT-00114?

PT-00114 is an investigational synthetic peptide developed by Protagenic Therapeutics (NASDAQ: PTIX), a University of Toronto spinout. It is a 41-amino acid synthetic analog of TCAP-1 — teneurin C-terminal associated peptide-1 — a naturally occurring neuropeptide involved in regulating the brain's response to stress through the CRF (corticotropin-releasing factor) pathway.

What makes PT-00114 scientifically interesting is where it acts: not at the end of the stress cascade, but at its beginning. Rather than sedating the nervous system broadly (benzodiazepines) or flooding serotonin synapses (SSRIs), PT-00114 inhibits CRH — the upstream hormonal signal that triggers the entire cortisol response.

Development Milestone: On November 11, 2026, Protagenic announced a private placement of up to $5 million to fund its first U.S. clinical trial for Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD). This follows positive Phase 1 safety results from ex-US studies and an FDA pre-IND Type B meeting in August 2026 that cleared the path to an IND submission.

Mechanism of Action

1. CRH Inhibition (HPA Axis)
The HPA axis is the body's primary stress-response circuit. When the brain perceives stress, the hypothalamus releases CRH, which triggers ACTH release from the pituitary, driving cortisol production in the adrenal glands. PT-00114 modulates the CRF pathway in an inhibitory manner — blunting the signal at the hypothalamic level before it cascades downstream.

2. Latrophilin (ADGRL/CIRL) GPCRs
Natural TCAP-1 also acts via latrophilins — adhesion GPCRs (ADGRL1, ADGRL2) expressed in stress-related brain regions including the amygdala, hippocampus, and hypothalamus. This may explain why PT-00114 shows activity in models where standard CRF1 receptor antagonists do not.

Key Research Findings

Al Chawaf et al. (2007, Behavioural Brain Research): Five days of IV TCAP-1 significantly decreased CRF-induced anxiety in both the open field test and elevated plus maze in rodents.

Tan et al. (2008, Psychoneuroendocrinology): TCAP-1 blocked CRF-induced increases in acoustic startle responses — a fear-sensitization measure relevant to PTSD research.

2026 Behavioural Pharmacology Study: Two days of PT-00114 reduced plasma corticosterone levels and attenuated anxiety-like behavior. Center-field time increased 282% versus controls (p=0.031). Effects were not replicated by a standard CRF1 antagonist in the same model.

Phase 1 Clinical Results (Ex-US): SAD and MAD studies in healthy volunteers completed September 2025 (Nuvisan GmbH, Germany, CTIS: 2024-519316-13-00). Topline results December 9, 2025: all cohorts completed, well-tolerated, no serious adverse events.

Why This Matters for Fitness, Recovery, and Longevity

  • Muscle catabolism: Elevated cortisol activates muscle protein breakdown via glucocorticoid receptors, blunting adaptation to resistance training.
  • Fat storage: Chronic cortisol drives visceral adipogenesis and insulin resistance.
  • Sleep disruption: CRF overactivation suppresses slow-wave sleep and blunts GH secretion.
  • Cognitive aging: Chronic cortisol accelerates hippocampal volume loss associated with memory decline and dementia risk.
  • Immune dysregulation: CRF/cortisol chronically suppresses cellular immunity while promoting low-grade inflammation.

FAQ

Q: What is PT-00114 and how is it different from existing anxiety treatments?
A: PT-00114 targets the upstream CRF signal — the initiating hormone in the HPA axis stress cascade — rather than broadly suppressing GABA (benzodiazepines) or globally affecting serotonin (SSRIs). This selectivity could mean a cleaner side-effect profile, though human efficacy evidence is still early-stage.

Q: What did the Phase 1 trial for PT-00114 show?
A: Completed ex-US Phase 1 SAD/MAD in healthy volunteers (December 2025 topline): well-tolerated across all cohorts, no serious adverse events. FDA pre-IND feedback (August 2026): no deficiencies. US IND targeted Q1 2027, first patient Q2 2027.

Q: Why is PT-00114 relevant to fitness and longevity?
A: Chronic CRF overactivation drives muscle catabolism, visceral fat gain, insulin resistance, sleep disruption, and hippocampal deterioration. PT-00114 targets CRH to reduce this cascade upstream without broad CNS suppression — a mechanistically rational approach for HPA-axis normalization in performance and longevity contexts.

Research Limitations

  • No published efficacy data in humans. Phase 1 results are safety/tolerability only.
  • US Phase 1/2a has not started; first patient dosing expected Q2 2027.
  • Direct receptor binding site not fully characterized in published literature.
  • Small-cap NASDAQ company (PTIX); timelines carry execution risk.
  • Prior Phase 2 PTSD guidance (2025) slipped; treat all timelines as subject to change.
